subject: [PATCH v8 10/30] mm: make PMD migration-entry splitting explicit

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch makes the splitting of PMD migration entries explicit by renaming the 'freeze' boolean in __split_huge_pmd() to 'to_migration_entries'. It also introduces a new function split_pmd_to_migration_entries() for use by try_to_migrate_one(). The patch asserts that only present or device-private PMDs are handed to this function. No functional changes are intended, and the patch is part of a larger series of 30 patches.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan noted that concurrent MADV_DONTNEED operations can zap the PMD migration entry or split it, potentially causing a ref leak due to the folio not being freed when split_huge_pmd_address(freeze=true) is called. They suggested considering a separate fix for this issue.

Reviewer noted that one potential issue in the patch is a refcount leak and suggested it be addressed separately.
reviews.raw_body:
Is it always a PMD migration entry? Can a concurrent MADV_DONTNEED zap
the PMD migration entry or split it with a partial zap? Although it
does not affect the correctness of the patch.

If that concurrent zap is possible, the existing code can leak a ref,
causing the folio to be not freed, since
split_huge_pmd_address(freeze=true) does not drop the folio refcount
when the PMD is zapped or becomes a PTE page.

We might want a separate fix for it.

Actually, Mika Penttilä's "migrate on fault for device pages"[1] also
talks about the race.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260924065313.899730-1-mpenttil@redhat.com

---

This part can be a separate fix for the refcount leak.

Otherwise, LGTM.


-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch makes the splitting of PMD migration entries explicit by renaming the 'freeze' boolean in __split_huge_pmd() to 'to_migration_entries'. It also introduces a new function split_pmd_to_migration_entries() that is used only by try_to_migrate_one(). The patch aims to clarify the purpose of the 'freeze' parameter and make the code more readable. Additionally, it adds an assertion in __split_huge_pmd_locked() to ensure that the PMD being split is either present or device-private.
